question.problem:
In a certain shop, eggs are sold in cartons by the dozen.
The weight of an egg, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $65\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $5\,\text{g},$ while the weight of an egg carton, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $50\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\text{g}.$
If one carton filled with eggs is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs more than $850\,\text{g}?$ You may assume that the weights are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ | $\,0.8508\,$ | $\,0.8531\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ | $\,0.8729\,$ | $\,0.8749\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ | $\,0.8925\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the weight of the $i$th egg, and let $Y$ denote the weight of a carton. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(65,{5}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 12,
$$

and

$$
Y∼N(50,{2}^{2}).
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the weight of a randomly selected carton filled with eggs. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{12}+Y,
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =12\cdot 65+50 \\  & =830, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =12\cdot {5}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\  & =304.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(830,304).
$$

In order to find $P(W>850),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>850) & =P(Z>\frac{850-830}{\sqrt{304}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1.15) \\  & =1-P(Z<1.15) \\  & =1-Φ(1.15)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.15)≈0.8749.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>850) & ≈1-Φ(1.15) \\  & ≈1-0.8749 \\  & =0.1251.\end{aligned}
$$
